summary: Accept Fractal wire names before changing client and peer senders

replay.detail: No claim replay or recovery behavior changes.

schema.detail: No persistent schema, data rewrite or generated model changes.

rules.detail: Replication signature domains, canonical signed bytes, checkpoint rules and digests remain unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Daemon client API requests accept fractal.client.v0 alongside st3.client.v0. Client WebSocket receivers accept fractal.client.* aliases and fractal.cap.* capabilities. Daemon and signed peer HTTP receivers accept x-fractal-* aliases; conflicting aliases or duplicate values are rejected. Senders retain old wire names until every fleet member accepts aliases. Generated client response decoders and schema annotation aliases are outside this server-first change.

downtime.detail: No coordinated restart or downtime is required; old clients and peers keep their deployed wire names throughout the accepting-release rollout.

manual.detail: No operator action or re-pairing is required. Bridge arn:lmig:smalltalk:2026-10-16-wire-fractal-accept-both has a sunset 60 days after the first release shipping it; sender cutover requires all members on an accepting release.

recovery.detail: Old sender output and persistent state remain unchanged, preserving swap-back before sender cutover.
